Most home service businesses in the Valley have no storefront. The office is a truck, the sales floor is a customer's driveway, and the phone in the cab is where every job starts. If you are looking for a web design company in Phoenix that builds for that kind of business, this page explains how we do it and what it costs. Dominion Web Design Pro writes every page by hand, shows you a free demo before you pay, and charges once: $497, $997 or $1,997.

The trades this page has in mind are the ones the desert keeps busy: air conditioning and heating, pool service, pest control, roofing, landscaping and irrigation. They share one problem. The customer is somewhere in a metro the size of a small state, and the website has to tell Google, and the customer, exactly where the crew will go.

Why a web design company in Phoenix should build for service areas, not an address

Google treats a business that travels to customers differently from a shop with a door. Its Business Profile guidelines say a service-area business, such as a plumber working from home, should hide its street address and list the areas it serves instead. You can name up to 20 of those areas by city or ZIP code, and you get one profile for the whole territory.

That leaves a gap the profile cannot fill. A list of cities on Google tells nobody what you do in Glendale or how fast you can reach Ahwatukee. The website is where that gets said. For a trade covering the Valley, the site plan matters more than the color scheme: a home page, a page for each service, and a page for each town or part of town you really cover, each one written about that place.

When the AC quits at three in the afternoon in July

Phoenix heat is not a figure of speech. The National Weather Service confirmed 2024 as the city's hottest year on record, with an average temperature of 78.6 degrees, and Sky Harbor reached 110 degrees or more on 70 days that year, against a typical 21. On September 25, 2024 it hit 113, the latest 110 degree day in the city's recorded history.

A homeowner with a dead condenser on a day like that is not reading your About page. They are standing in a hot kitchen with a phone, comparing two or three results, and calling the first one that looks real and answers. A pool owner with green water before a weekend party behaves the same way, and so does someone who just found scorpions in the garage. The site has one job in that moment.

  • A tap-to-call number at the top of every screen, not buried below the fold.
  • The service and the area in the first line: "AC repair in Maryvale and west Phoenix," not "Welcome to our website."
  • Pages that load fast on a phone signal in a parking lot.
  • A short form for the customer who would rather type than talk, emailed straight to you.
  • Hours stated plainly, including whether you take emergency calls.

The Valley is too big for a single page

The city of Phoenix alone covers about 518 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau estimated 1,673,164 residents there in July 2024. The city divides itself into 15 urban villages for planning, with names such as Maryvale, Alhambra, Central City, South Mountain and North Gateway, and residents use those names when they describe where they live.

Then come the suburbs, each a large city in its own right. The same 2024 Census estimates put Mesa at 517,151 people, Gilbert at 288,790, Chandler at 281,231, Glendale at 258,143, Scottsdale at 246,170 and Peoria at 199,924. A pest control company based in Gilbert and a landscaper based in Peoria may never cross paths, and a homeowner in Chandler types "Chandler" into the search box, not "Phoenix."

A page plan for one Valley trade

Here is how we would sketch a site for a pool service that works the East Valley. The real plan comes from your own service list and the towns where your trucks actually go.

PageWhat it says
HomeWeekly pool service and repairs across the East Valley, the call button, and the towns covered.
Weekly serviceWhat a visit includes, how often, and what you check each time.
Green pool cleanupThe urgent job, written for the person searching on a Friday afternoon.
Equipment repairPumps, filters and heaters you work on, and what you do not touch.
Mesa, Gilbert, Chandler pagesOne page each, about that city: which parts you cover and how scheduling works there.
ContactPhone, form, hours and the service area in plain words.

We do not sell page counts. Ten pages that each answer a real search will do more for a crew than a hundred thin ones with the town name swapped.

Web design in Phoenix for licensed trades: show the ROC number

Arizona gives homeowners an easy way to check a contractor, and careful ones use it. The Arizona Registrar of Contractors says that when a whole project, labor and materials together, costs $1,000 or more, or needs a city permit, the person doing the work must hold a contractor license. Calling yourself a handyman does not change that. The ROC's public contractor search looks up a license by its six-digit number or by name, and only a current, active license may legally contract.

If you are licensed, that is a selling point most trade websites waste. Put the ROC number in the footer of every page and on the contact page, say what your license classification covers, and link to the state's search so a cautious customer can check you in thirty seconds. It costs nothing, and it answers the question a homeowner who has been burned before is already asking.

What we ask a Phoenix trade before writing a word

Which towns do your trucks really reach in a normal week? Which job pays best, and which one do you wish you could stop taking? Do you answer after hours, and who picks up? What is your ROC number and classification? The answers shape the page list, and the first screen of the home page comes straight out of them.

Everything is done by phone, email and shared links. You read every page before it goes live and change what is wrong.

Which package fits a crew that covers the Valley

A one-truck operation working a few nearby ZIP codes can start with Starter at $497: five hand-written pages, the contact form, map and hours, and titles and a sitemap submitted to Google, live in 7 to 14 days. A company running several trucks across three or four cities usually fits Pro at $997, because its ten city pages let Mesa, Tempe or Glendale each get a page of its own. Pro also adds Google Business Profile setup, schema markup and your Google reviews on the site. Its AI chat widget, which answers visitors around the clock and takes a name and number, is free for 14 days and then $297 a month.

Agency at $1,997 is for the business that wants the whole map. It starts with keyword research across your service area, then builds a page for every town and service pairing the research supports, usually 30 to 60 pages, in waves with the first live inside two weeks. It includes setup of an AI phone agent; the agent itself is free for 7 days and then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, and you can cancel any time. That monthly fee is separate from the one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep an AI agent, or $49 a month without one. The pricing page lists every item.

Built in East Texas for a desert business

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Phoenix. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

Nobody here will pretend to know Valley summers the way you do. What we bring is the writing and the build; what you bring is which neighborhoods call you most and which jobs you want more of.

Where Valley owners get free business help

  • Maricopa SBDCThe Small Business Development Center led by Maricopa Community Colleges offers advising at no cost and mostly free workshops for businesses at every stage.
  • Greater Phoenix ChamberRuns business retention and expansion visits with the Arizona Commerce Authority, the City of Phoenix and Maricopa County, connecting owners to resources such as the SBDC.
  • City of PhoenixThe city's Small Business Support Division runs its small business certification for city contracts, and its Neighborhood Services Department lists free management and technical assistance for small businesses.
  • SCORE in ArizonaVolunteer mentors offer free mentoring and workshops in Phoenix and around the state.
  • Arizona Registrar of ContractorsThe licensing agency's public search is the place to confirm your own license shows as current before you link to it.

Common questions

What do Phoenix web design services usually include?

It depends on who you hire, so ask for the list in writing. With Dominion Web Design Pro the list is printed: Starter ($497 one time) is five hand-written pages, a contact form that emails every lead, Google Maps and hours, titles and a sitemap submitted to Google, and the site is yours. Pro ($997) adds ten pages, a photo gallery, local SEO setup with schema and Google Business Profile, your Google reviews on the site and ten city pages. Agency ($1,997) adds keyword research across your whole service area and a page for each town and service worth having.

How much does a web design company in Phoenix charge?

Quotes across the Valley run from a few hundred dollars for a template to many thousands for an agency build, often with a monthly fee on top. Our prices are $497, $997 and $1,997, paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it.

Can one website cover Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert and Scottsdale too?

Yes, and it should if you work there. The usual way is a separate page for each city you serve, written about that city and the jobs you do there, not one page with a long list of town names. Pro includes ten city pages; Agency researches the whole service area first and usually lands at 30 to 60 pages, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks.

Should a mobile service business show its home address on Google?

Google's own guidelines say a service-area business that does not serve customers at its address should hide that address and list the areas it covers instead, using up to 20 service areas. Your website then does the job of explaining which towns and which jobs you take.

Are you a web development company in Phoenix?

No. Dominion Web Design Pro is one person, Maurice Johnson, working from Big Sandy in East Texas. He writes and builds every site himself and delivers it remotely. If you want a Phoenix firm you can visit in person, that is a fair reason to hire one.
